spec.full_target: Let n,m be positive integers. Let u:R^n times (0,infinity) -> R^m be jointly smooth, and let q in R^m have Euclidean norm one. Assume: for every x and t>0, |u(x,t)|=1; at each (x,t), u_tt-Delta_x u=a(x,t)u for some real a; and on every compact interval J contained in (0,infinity), u(x,t)=q outside a compact C_J, uniformly for t in J. Define e(x,t)=|u_t|^2+sum_j|partial_(x_j)u|^2 and E(t)=integral_R^n e(x,t) dx with Lebesgue measure. Prove e(.,t) integrable for each t>0, E differentiable at every t>0, and E'(t)=0. No endpoint assertion at 0.
spec.conclusion: For every r>0, e(.,r) is Lebesgue integrable, E is differentiable at r, and E'(r)=0.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary r0>0. Choose δ with 0<δ<r0 and set J=[r0−δ,r0+δ]. This is a compact interval contained in (0,∞) with r0 interior; record this as F001.

produces.statement: There exists a compact interval J⊂(0,∞) with r0 in its interior.

argument.text: Choose J by F001, and apply H003 to obtain C_J. On the exterior of C_J the function u is constant q on J, so its time derivative is zero in the interior of J; its spatial derivatives vanish on the open exterior and, by continuity, on the boundary. Thus e(·,t) is continuous and supported in C_J for t∈J. Apply M001 to e(·,r0): Euclidean Lebesgue space has measurable opens and measure finite on compact sets; R is a normed additive commutative group. This proves integrability. Choose a closed box B containing C_J. On B×J, e_t is continuous. The product is compact, so M004 applied to e_t gives uniform continuity there. For fixed x∈B, M002 applied to t↦e(x,t), with derivative e_t(x,t), gives the difference quotient as the oriented interval average of e_t. Continuity gives interval integrability and differentiability. Uniform continuity implies these quotients converge uniformly in x to e_t(x,r0). Since B has finite Lebesgue measure, their integrals converge to ∫_B e_t(x,r0)dx, proving E differentiable at r0 and E'(r0)=∫_B e_t(x,r0)dx.

Differentiate the finite sum defining e to get e_t=2u_t·u_tt+2Σ_j u_j·∂_j u_t. For each j put g_j(x)=u_t(x,r0)·u_j(x,r0). It is smooth with compact support in C_J and ∂_j g_j=(∂_j u_t)·u_j+u_t·u_jj. The derivative is continuous and compactly supported, hence integrable by M001. Identify R^n with R×R^(n−1) by the coordinate permutation; the product Lebesgue measures are S-finite, and the coordinate identification preserves Lebesgue integration, so M003 applies to this integrable function. Fubini reduces its integral to integrating first along x_j. For each fixed remaining coordinate, M002 on a finite interval containing the support of g_j says the integral of ∂_j g_j is the endpoint difference, zero. Therefore ∫(∂_j u_t)·u_j=−∫u_t·u_jj. Summing gives E'(r0)=2∫u_t·(u_tt−Δ_xu). Differentiating H001 in time yields u·u_t=0. H002 says the acceleration is a scalar multiple of u, so pointwise u_t·(u_tt−Δ_xu)=0. The integrand is continuous and supported in C_J; its integral is zero. Hence E'(r0)=0.
Because r0>0 was arbitrary, the integrability, differentiability and zero derivative established above hold at every positive time. No assertion at r=0 is made.
